# Advisories accepted for now, one id per line (GHSA-... or PYSEC-...).
#
# Every entry needs a comment saying why it is accepted and what would close it.
# An entry with no expiry condition is a standing risk, not an ignore -- those
# are also recorded in docs/accepted-risks.md, so they are reviewed with the rest.
#
# This is a BASELINE, not a mute: the job still fails on any advisory not listed
# here, including a new one against the same package.

# --- starlette 0.46.2, reached only through services/vault/requirements.txt ---
#
# starlette is not a direct dependency anywhere in this repository; it arrives
# through fastapi. The vault is the only component with a stale upper cap
# (fastapi>=0.111,<0.116), which resolves fastapi 0.115.14 -> starlette 0.46.2.
# Its siblings use <0.141 or are uncapped and resolve clean, which is why
# exactly one of the 16 requirements files fails.
#
# Verified on Python 3.12.3 with clean resolves of both sides: relaxing that cap
# to <0.141 gives fastapi 0.140.13 -> starlette 1.6.0, above every fix version
# below, with a byte-identical OpenAPI surface (same 23 paths).
#
# Not done in the change that introduced this check, because the vault has no
# Python test job in ci.yml at all -- only the two migration jobs, which
# exercise schema SQL rather than the service -- so the bump would land in the
# secret store unverified. Its own suite cannot close that gap either:
# tests/test_contract_smoke.py needs the live endpoint caj-vault-smoke-test
# runs against, and requirements-test.txt is missing opentelemetry-sdk, so
# tests/test_telemetry_wiring.py cannot even be collected as committed.
#
# CLOSES WHEN: services/vault's fastapi cap is raised to <0.141 in BOTH
# requirements.txt and pyproject.toml (the cap is declared twice and nothing
# keeps the two in sync; pip-audit only reads the former), alongside a vault
# test job in ci.yml that makes the bump verifiable. Delete this whole block in
# that same change -- if the cap moves and these lines stay, the job goes on
# accepting advisories that no longer apply.
#
# Accepted by the repository owner on PR #128; see docs/accepted-risks.md.
